  "text": "Tobias Reel came down from the church when the bell let him.\n\nThe tide was where a tide should be. There were gulls, four of them, working a line of weed on the flat, and a wind off the land that smelled of peat smoke. The light had a source again. He looked at it, the sun, low over the headland, as if to be sure.\n\nHe did not go onto the beach. He went along the top of the dune where the path was, and he counted the posts because his hands wanted something to count. Eleven. The eleventh stood by her porch with a rime of salt on its north face, dry, ordinary, the way a post is.\n\nThe door was shut. He had expected that. The lamp stood on the sill, unlit, and there was the chip in its base that he had known since her father bought it. He put his palm flat to the glass of the window. Cold, and the room behind it dim: the boards, the rug, the two chairs. Nothing moved and nothing was out of place and nothing was wet.\n\nHe stood there a long while, longer than he meant, with his hand on the window.\n\nThen, because he was old and had learned what was his to do and what was not, he turned to the water.
